Compact cyclic detector and exact matrix-oracle learner
Statement: Interface: proper characteristic-zero recognizable series f on n symbols, hidden-state bound m; exact FULL matrix-output oracle, not passive samples. Explicit Volterra T_i dimension2nm; f≠0⇒f(ℓT_1,…,ℓT_n)≠0 for someℓ∈{1,…,m}. Direct-sum dimension2nm²; acyclic full-output case one unscaled2nm tuple suffices. Joint strict triangularity makes evaluations legal.
Proof mechanism: released116 finite-word hyperlog independence→bivariate Volterra kernel→covariant rational row span detects a nonzero diagonal derivative before m→degree bounds/Cauchy interpolation→small scalar grid. Exact alias AB−B(I+A)^−1A(I+B) has leading commutator but vanishes at unscaled J_1,J_2 at EVERY truncation; greater dimension alone fails.
Learner: minimal r≤m realization, ≤m(1+nr) exact matrix queries of dimension≤2nm(r+1), feature length4n²m³. Residual combinations share transitions (m bound); unrelated hypothesis comparison may need2m. Independent batched width2n: maxdimension2n(m+r)≤4nm, calls≤m+nm²r. Charge full output entries, coefficient heights, elimination, execution/stability; field arithmetic≠bit time; no positive stochastic realization guarantee.
Critical novelty correction: release116+routine truncation/unrolling/length marker ALREADY implies polynomial proper-cyclic capability at O(nm^5) query dimension. Increment=compactness/charged query tradeoff, not first post-release polynomial learnability. Pre-release comparator quasipolynomial; scaling/output-only learning old. Practical useful oracle acquisition and independent proof/priority remain open.
Evidence reported:9adversarial fixtures×2modes,18 exact all-word/minimal-rank checks,1230 queries/1847592 returned field entries; cyclic rank4:45calls/dim80 vs205calls/dim32,batched slower. Other3fixtures75queries14.40s;14-query discriminator1.516s/75264inputbits/42359responsebits. Not a universal execution benchmark.

Joint strict triangularity makes evaluations legal.

One receiver per frame direction gives a simultaneous canonical measurement score
Statement: A depth-m binary broadcaster tree has every receiver marginal Phi^m. Pulling back simultaneous spectral PVMs produces one POVM M and canonical EB map Psi_M(X)=sum_z tau(M_z X)M_z/tau(M_z), tau=Tr/d, with <A_i,Psi_M A_i>_tau >= 2<A_i,Phi^m A_i>_tau-||A_i||_2,tau^2 for ALL frame elements simultaneously. Phi CPTP, unital and HS self-adjoint; a CPTP two-output broadcaster has both marginals Phi. No HS-positive-spectrum premise; spectrum may lie anywhere in [-1,1]. Zero POVM effects omitted; no output side record acquired. For every d>=2, supplied self-compatible Phi on M_d, and every Hermitian frame A_1,...,A_r with r<=d^2; m=ceil(log2(d^2)), K=2^m.
Requires: Explicit finite-dimensional Phi and broadcaster; frame supplied.
Returns: One input POVM and common frame score; not independent choices for different directions.

One receiver per frame direction gives a simultaneous canonical measurement score

Obstruction: Separate frame-specific POVMs do not yield a universal comparator. Receiver reuse across directions is not justified; cost grows with frame dimension.
Requires: Explicit finite-dimensional Phi and broadcaster; frame supplied.

Compact convex separation upgrades all-frame witnesses to one channel
Statement: I-Psi <=_HS 2m(I-Phi). For rho_H=(I+H)/d, ||H||_infinity<=theta<1, r=sup_H||Phi(H)-H||_1,tau, the SAME Psi satisfies sup_H T(Psi(rho_H),rho_H)<=sqrt(2m theta r)/2. All-frame score witnesses from LA001. Cone order is on the real Hermitian HS space, not matrix Loewner order on density operators. Tr H=0 and rho_H are states; half-trace normalization. For every supplied channel satisfying LA001, there EXISTS one full-domain canonical EB Psi; d>=2, m=ceil(log2(d^2)).
Requires: Supplied broadcaster and channel; optional bounded tracial likelihood family.
Returns: Existential one common EB comparator; logarithmic-dimensional loss.

Compact convex separation upgrades all-frame witnesses to one channel
Returns: Existential one common EB comparator; logarithmic-dimensional loss.

Obstruction: r log d->0 is sufficient; bounded Holevo does not imply it. Failure in canonical measurement subclass would not rule out arbitrary EB comparators. No dimension-free constant or hardware compiler follows.

Bounded SLD score turns reconstruction loss into commutator energy
Statement: With e=int T(rho_x,Phi rho_x), L_x=sigma^-1/2 rho_x sigma^-1/2, G_x=L_x(A+L_x)^-1, B_i=A_i sqrt(sigma): A sum_i int ||[G_x,B_i]||_HS^2 <= (5/2)e. No output commutation, covariance, unitality, reference preservation, dimension or largest-likelihood factor. Finite-dimensional measurable ensemble with common strictly positive mean. Source states commute with mean; output xi=Phi(sigma) may be singular/noncommuting. Half-trace error and identical source/output Hilbert space as stated. For any finite-dimensional trace-one ensemble rho_x with mean sigma>0, [rho_x,sigma]=0 EVERY x, ANY CPTP Phi with Kraus A_i, and EVERY public scalar A>0.
Requires: Source ensemble, analytic mean, reconstruction channel; bounded effect witnesses used in proof.
Returns: Operational lower-bound Dirichlet energy for rank-Q hybrid composite Kraus refinements.

Bounded SLD score turns reconstruction loss into commutator energy
Returns: Operational lower-bound Dirichlet energy for rank-Q hybrid composite Kraus refinements.
Conditions: Finite-dimensional measurable ensemble with common strictly positive mean. Source states commute with mean; output xi=Phi(sigma) may be singular/noncommuting. Half-trace error and identical source/output Hilbert space as stated.
Obstruction: Cropping G to output support deletes essential positive cross terms. Accuracy on rho_x does not imply accuracy on artificial sigma G_x experiment. Different means cannot share one score argument; arbitrary noncommuting means not covered.
Requires: Source ensemble, analytic mean, reconstruction channel; bounded effect witnesses used in proof.

Legal input pinching preserves exact right-modulus mass and simultaneous energies
Statement: Refine input-pinched Kraus A_(i,mu)=A_i P_mu; B=A_(i,mu)sqrt(sigma). Selected F_z=|B|/sqrt2 for mu in C have rank<=Q, one-source-sector support, sum_z F_z^2=sigma P_C/2 and total HS mass Tr(sigma P_C)/2. Paired SVD inequality gives selected commutator energy <= FULL REFINED Kraus energy simultaneously for every field. Input pinching fixes actual targets and does not raise maximum branch dimension. For bounded operational score bound add source-mean commutation and LA003. Same sigma/channel for all mixed ensembles; non-block fields retain refined RHS indexing. For finite H=direct_sum_mu H_mu, EVERY block-diagonal target ensemble with sigma>0, ANY reconstruction through maximum conditional branch Q, ANY source subset C, and ANY finite collection of Hermitian score fields.
Requires: Exact source sector decomposition and TP reconstruction; chosen C is proof-term subset.
Returns: Positive matrices for converse; not a trace-preserving selected code or conditioned experiment.

Legal input pinching preserves exact right-modulus mass and simultaneous energies
Returns: Positive matrices for converse; not a trace-preserving selected code or conditioned experiment.
Conditions: Input pinching fixes actual targets and does not raise maximum branch dimension. For bounded operational score bound add source-mean commutation and LA003. Same sigma/channel for all mixed ensembles; non-block fields retain refined RHS indexing.
Obstruction: Right modulus alone need not reduce energy; favorable orientation alone need not preserve source mass. Selecting terms is not deleting source states or conditioning on C. No blanket rectangular-sector, code or total-memory-optimality theorem.
Requires: Exact source sector decomposition and TP reconstruction; chosen C is proof-term subset.

Isometric-bundle path heat bound retains holonomy and yields discrete Nash
Statement: H_M uses K_M=d_M|<v,w>|^(2M), d_M=(M+1)(M+2)/2; B_t=H_M^t exp[-t C_V/k^2]. ||B_t||_(1->infinity)<=430 d_M k^2/t^3. ||g||_2^2<=t(E_H+E_V/k^2)+h_B(t)||g||_1^2. General path kernel bound h_X(t)h_V(s) requires compatible fiber isometries, not flatness. Transport inverses/isometries and invariant vertical heat; reversibility for Nash. C_V spherical eigenvalues ell(ell+1); H_M strongly commutes with vertical heat. Discrete integer powers; H_M HS spectrum may be negative. M>=1,k>=1 integers; X=CP2, fiber CP1 with probability measures, actual reversible unitary plane transports; EVERY integer 1<=t<=min(M+1,k^2); every g in L2 with finite vertical energy.
Requires: Explicit base kernel, geometric transports and analytic fiber heat.
Returns: Connection-retaining scalar smoothing/Nash bound with actual finite time window.

Isometric-bundle path heat bound retains holonomy and yields discrete Nash
Returns: Connection-retaining scalar smoothing/Nash bound with actual finite time window.
Conditions: Transport inverses/isometries and invariant vertical heat; reversibility for Nash. C_V spherical eigenvalues ell(ell+1); H_M strongly commutes with vertical heat. Discrete integer powers; H_M HS spectrum may be negative.
Obstruction: beta_0=1 prevents extending pure t^-2 estimate beyond acquired window. Integrated coherent-symbol contraction does not hold pointwise. Cannot multiply cold and hot memory bounds without SAME-symbol contracts.
Requires: Explicit base kernel, geometric transports and analytic fiber heat.

Continuous no-jump term makes full-space smoothing norm infinite
Statement: For A=(I-H_M)+C_V/k^2, ||exp(-tA)||_(1->infinity)=infinity. The positive zero-horizontal-jump term e^-t V_(t/k^2) preserves arbitrarily concentrated base mass. Non-atomic CP2 base and fiber-constant functions. Poisson continuous semigroup has positive j=0 term. For the same continuous scalar flag space and EVERY finite t>0.
Requires: Concentrated base indicator g_B=1_B/dv(B), ||g_B||_1=1.
Returns: Exact falsifier of an unqualified full-space continuous smoothing bound.

Sector anti-concentration amplifies a single trial into a partition lower bound
Statement: Z_I=Tr_I exp(-tau B) >= (q/pmax) exp[-tau <psi_I,B psi_I>], psi_I=P_I psi/sqrt q. No upper bound on individual sector energies is required. For Poisson-binomial trial number, pmax<=sqrt(pi)/(2sqrt(2V)) with V=sum rho_i(1-rho_i). [B,P_m]=0 gives exact sector orthogonality and energy decomposition. Jensen applied to each normalized sector and then conditional weights p_m/q. Poisson-binomial estimate needs independent Bernoulli occupation parameters, not identical ones. Any finite Hermitian B commuting with orthogonal sector projectors P_m, unit trial psi, tau>0, any sector subset I with q=sum_I p_m>0 and pmax=max_m p_m; p_m=||P_m psi||^2.
Requires: Analytic trial vector, sector weights/maximum mass and projected energy.
Returns: Trace/partition lower bound; not exact weights or upper asymptotics.

Sector anti-concentration amplifies a single trial into a partition lower bound
Returns: Trace/partition lower bound; not exact weights or upper asymptotics.
Conditions: [B,P_m]=0 gives exact sector orthogonality and energy decomposition. Jensen applied to each normalized sector and then conditional weights p_m/q. Poisson-binomial estimate needs independent Bernoulli occupation parameters, not identical ones.
Obstruction: A single projected trial alone yields only exp(-tau E), losing sector entropy. Does not imply exact partition asymptotics or profile mixture weights.
Requires: Analytic trial vector, sector weights/maximum mass and projected energy.

Exact ghost endpoints remove O(1) scaled-energy bias
Statement: For product theta_i=theta(i/L) with ghost theta_0=theta_L=0, endpoint killing fields exactly complete missing bonds. <Hcrit>=J sum_(i=0)^(L-1)[1-cos Delta theta_i], <W>=sum rho_i²-(1/2)sum(Delta rho_i)². <B_L>=L E(theta)+O(C_theta/L). Bounded shifts kappa+zeta_L/L,lambda+eta_L/L change trial energy to -zeta_L int rho²-eta_L int rho+o(1). Hcrit=J sum interior(I-sigma dot sigma)+J(I-Z1)+J(I-ZS); A_L=L² Hcrit, B_L=A_L-kappa W-lambda N. Smooth theta and rho have zero endpoint values; continuum minimizer energy zero. Acquiring/certifying lambda_* and minimizer is separate from analytic existence. Fixed J,tau>0,kappa>2J pi²/3, lambda=lambda_*(kappa); smooth nonzero zero-energy Dirichlet minimizer theta with rho=sin²(theta/2); S=L-1 physical sites, BOTH endpoint fields.
Requires: Explicit lattice/continuum model with fixed parameters and analytic minimizer.
Returns: O(1/L) scaled trial bias and sufficient bounded-detuning robustness.

Exact ghost endpoints remove O(1) scaled-energy bias
Returns: O(1/L) scaled trial bias and sufficient bounded-detuning robustness.
Conditions: Hcrit=J sum interior(I-sigma dot sigma)+J(I-Z1)+J(I-ZS); A_L=L² Hcrit, B_L=A_L-kappa W-lambda N. Smooth theta and rho have zero endpoint values; continuum minimizer energy zero. Acquiring/certifying lambda_* and minimizer is separate from analytic existence.
Obstruction: Dropping either endpoint changes model and can restore hidden O(1) scaled bias. O(1/L) robust window is only sufficient; shifts a logL/L need separate analysis. No sharp finite-size width or exact coexistence weights.
Requires: Explicit lattice/continuum model with fixed parameters and analytic minimizer.

Odd-degree closed-left-half-plane endpoint inequality
Statement: a_0 a_d<=a_1 a_(d-1). Middle coefficient sign assumption unnecessary. Multiplicities and imaginary-axis roots allowed. This endpoint inequality is established prior in cited Anari et al. Lemma 28/Asner mechanism according to source; exact imported original theorem was not reopened in this extraction. Odd actual degree, real coefficients, positive nonzero endpoints, closed left-half-plane roots. EVERY real polynomial p(z)=sum_(j=0)^d a_j z^j of ODD degree d with a_0,a_d>0 and no root in Re z>0.
Requires: Polynomial or exact coefficient/root-domain proof.
Returns: Endpoint coefficient comparison usable after stable univariate reduction.

Odd-degree closed-left-half-plane endpoint inequality
Returns: Endpoint coefficient comparison usable after stable univariate reduction.
Conditions: Odd actual degree, real coefficients, positive nonzero endpoints, closed left-half-plane roots.
Obstruction: Even-degree p=1+z² defeats conclusion; oddness is load-bearing. Do not present alternate elementary proof as a new inequality.
Requires: Polynomial or exact coefficient/root-domain proof.

Reciprocal twist and weighted fields give coefficient-one square-root exchange
Statement: sqrt(f(S)f(T)) <= sum_(j in D,j!=a) sqrt(f(S xor {a,j}) f(T xor {a,j})); optimal universal leading constant one. Zero endpoint cases immediate and S=T has no a. No homogeneity, determinant representation, genericity or log-concavity premise. Multiaffinity, constant parity, nonnegative coefficients and right-half-plane stability. Signed real-stable upper-half-plane polynomial transfers only under explicit i-rotation as in source. Finite E; nonzero multiaffine h(x)=sum_U f(U)x^U, f>=0 supported on ONE parity, h(z)!=0 whenever Re z_i>0. EVERY S,T in supported parity and EVERY a in D=S symmetric_difference T.
Requires: Exact stable coefficient family; common occupied core remains in coefficient data.
Returns: Aggregate exchange bound, support symmetric-exchange implication.

Reciprocal twist and weighted fields give coefficient-one square-root exchange
Returns: Aggregate exchange bound, support symmetric-exchange implication.
Conditions: Multiaffinity, constant parity, nonnegative coefficients and right-half-plane stability. Signed real-stable upper-half-plane polynomial transfers only under explicit i-rotation as in source.
Obstruction: Squaring gives square of sum, NOT already-refuted coefficient-one sum of squares. Aggregate support exchange does not select low-energy microscopic exchanges or bound two-replica ratios. Drop parity and endpoint reduction fails; unsigned upper-half-plane stability not inferred.
Requires: Exact stable coefficient family; common occupied core remains in coefficient data.

Energy-ordered triangular inverse preserves hard legality
Statement: Order energy basis increasingly, E=Tdag T upper Cholesky,B=T^-1,P=1_[0,Q](sum_i H_i). Exact legal miss minimum p_n(Q)=||B^tensor n P||^-2. For any legal unit y, chi=B^tensor n y/||B^tensor n y|| is legal with that vector miss. Tilted norms/order thresholds are invariant under bases within degenerate energy blocks. Parallel zero-false-alarm pure-null test; no retained ancilla or adaptive interventions. Hard support rho=P rho P; expected-energy ceiling is different. Full rank E and unique ground; noninteracting sum Hamiltonian. Known finite D>=2, H>=0 with unique ground |0>, 0<E<=I and E|0>=|0>; EVERY n>=1,Q>=0.
Requires: Explicit calibrated miss effect, energy eigenbasis and upper Cholesky factor.
Returns: Constrained many-copy optimization becomes tensor inverse-norm problem; legal constructive witness.

Energy-ordered triangular inverse preserves hard legality
Returns: Constrained many-copy optimization becomes tensor inverse-norm problem; legal constructive witness.
Conditions: Parallel zero-false-alarm pure-null test; no retained ancilla or adaptive interventions. Hard support rho=P rho P; expected-energy ceiling is different. Full rank E and unique ground; noninteracting sum Hamiltonian.
Obstruction: Typical projection for -log E need not meet hard H support. No expected-cost or singular-effect transfer. Additional vacuum slots reduce to at most floor(Q/hmin) excited sites, not hidden infinite input resource.

Uniform polynomial-probability type rounding yields exact legal probes
Statement: There exists count k summing n with exact multinomial mass p_type>=exp(-C_D)(n+1)^-D and |sum k_j h_j-n sum p_j h_j|<=K. Combined with top tilted vector and LA011: ng(c)-2s_h K-D log(n+1)-C_D<=-log p_n(nc)<=ng(c), simultaneously every c>=0; g(c)=inf_s>=0[log||e^-sH/2 BdagB e^-sH/2||+sc]. Fixed finite D, probabilities may be arbitrarily small or zero. Tilt geometry supplies a top vector of desired mean; hard contract of LA011 for detection consequence. Nonlattice energies and degenerate energy levels allowed. EVERY probability vector p on <=D coordinates, every n>=1 and energies 0<=h_j<=hmax. K=(D-1)hmax,C_D=(D-1)+D(D-1)².
Requires: p,n,energy values; in application calibrated matrices and dual minimizing tilt.
Returns: One EXACT total-energy type with polynomial mass; uniform O(log n) remainder.

Uniform polynomial-probability type rounding yields exact legal probes
Returns: One EXACT total-energy type with polynomial mass; uniform O(log n) remainder.

A weak-signal proper score recovers linear TV-to-feature distortion
Statement: Posterior p_r(x)=(1+tanh(rx))/2; u_r(p)=tanh(arctanh(2p-1)/r). Bounded proper loss in [0,1] from convex antiderivative F_r satisfies D_F(p,q)>=r|u_r(p)-u_r(q)|²/4. With u_r(p_r(x))=tanh x, under common null P0, E(tanh X_i-tanh Y_i)²<=4sqrt(e)epsilon/r, and I(X_i;Y_i,S)>=.5 log(r/epsilon)-1.25-log2. Decoder independent of unknown mean/sign; Markov T-(X,S)-Y_i. Independent public seed allowed; accuracy only seed-average. Same measurable stored state and own scalar query output; null law is analytic reference, no reconstruction requirement at theta0. X~N(theta,I_d), 0<r<=1; blind same archive before coordinate i is chosen; each query decoder reconstructs ONLY scalar laws at theta=+/-r e_i within TV epsilon.
Requires: Sparse Gaussian alternative pairs and chosen coordinate query.
Returns: Weak-signal linear epsilon/r distortion bound; scalar information demand.

Returns: Weak-signal linear epsilon/r distortion bound; scalar information demand.

SSA charges incompatible later measurements to the same quantum memory
Statement: sum_i I(X_i;Y_i,S)<=log D although the Y_i need not admit a joint measurement or sequential readout. Combined LA013 gives log D>=d/2 log(r/epsilon)-(5/4+log2)d. Source coordinate independence conditional at each independent seed. All input-dependent classical branches count in D=sum d_j; largest branch is insufficient here. Standard Borel spaces; state entries/POVM effects measurable. Query arrives after encoding and reveals coordinate, not unknown sign. Finite d independent null coordinates X_i, independent public seed S, measurable same retained direct-sum quantum state of total dimension <=D each seed; each later chosen query i may use its own incompatible POVM.
Requires: One stored state supporting every possible one-shot coordinate query.
Returns: Memory converse without simultaneous output assumption.

SSA charges incompatible later measurements to the same quantum memory
Returns: Memory converse without simultaneous output assumption.
Conditions: Source coordinate independence conditional at each independent seed. All input-dependent classical branches count in D=sum d_j; largest branch is insufficient here. Standard Borel spaces; state entries/POVM effects measurable. Query arrives after encoding and reveals coordinate, not unknown sign.
Obstruction: Single-POVM trace bound alone does not justify incompatible-output sum. Encoder knowing query in advance could store only one coordinate; theorem fails. No assertion that memory survives another destructive query. SSA/Holevo/random-access mechanism is established prior; original cited papers not reread here.
Requires: One stored state supporting every possible one-shot coordinate query.

Finite affine active slopes approximate exponent vectors with discontinuous tolerance
Statement: There exists finite nonempty h-independent slope family r_lambda in[a,b]^m with offsets b_lambda(h)=o(h^a). If h_n->0+,p^n in R^m->p in[a,b]^m and a FIXED label lambda is active at X_hn(p^n)=(h_n^p_i^n)_i for every n, then ||p-r_lambda||_infinity<E(r_lambda). All weakly tied minimizers active; approximating p^n need not be inside cube. Finite nonempty affine lower envelope and positive tolerance at each slope. Offsets defined on common sufficiently small interval; no continuity required in h. EVERY integer m>=1, reals a<b and arbitrary E:[a,b]^m->(0,infinity), without regularity.
Requires: Dimension,cube and full arbitrary positive tolerance function.
Returns: Existential finite family with sequential active-slope guarantee.

Finite affine active slopes approximate exponent vectors with discontinuous tolerance
Returns: Existential finite family with sequential active-slope guarantee.
Conditions: Finite nonempty affine lower envelope and positive tolerance at each slope. Offsets defined on common sufficiently small interval; no continuity required in h.
Obstruction: Approximate vectors outside cube are necessary for boundary induction; clipping them changes guarantee. Rational exponents/continuity cannot be assumed to obtain effective cutoff. This geometry alone supplies neither reaction drift nor global positive absorber.
Requires: Dimension,cube and full arbitrary positive tolerance function.

Fix the affine family before extracting a uniform small-scale activity cutoff
Statement: ||p-r_lambda||_infinity<E(r_lambda) uniformly in p and all ties. Family and its finite slope set are fixed BEFORE h0 is chosen; no continuity of E is needed. LA015 sequential guarantee, finite family and compact exponent cube. For each family Lambda supplied by LA015 with m>=1,a<b and E>0, there EXISTS h0 in(0,1); EVERY 0<h<h0,EVERY p in[a,b]^m and EVERY active lambda at X_h(p).
Requires: One already fixed affine family and tolerance values at its slopes.
Returns: Existential uniform activity cutoff; not a numerically acquired bound.

Fix the affine family before extracting a uniform small-scale activity cutoff

For each finite channel \(\mathcal N:A\to B\), let \(J\) be its unnormalized Choi matrix and \(J^+\) its Moore–Penrose inverse. The manuscript claims that one Choi objective
\[
 M(\mathcal N)=\min_{\sigma\in\mathcal D(B)}\left\|\operatorname{Tr}_B[(I\otimes\sigma)J^+(I\otimes\sigma)]\right\|_\infty,
 \qquad \operatorname{ran}(I\otimes\sigma)\subseteq\operatorname{ran}J,

gives \(\eta_{D_f}^c=\eta_{D_f}^{\Delta}=\eta_{I_f}=1-M^{-1}\) for (i) nonaffine modular Petz generators normalized by \(f(1)=f'(1)=0\), operator convex, with \(f(0+)<\infty\), and finite \(\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)/x\); the same equality is claimed for each fixed Petz Rényi order \(0<\alpha<1\) and quantum Chernoff divergence. Orthogonal-unitary noise has an exact inverse-probability Choi objective and shortest-word decay law
Statement: Claim (source-reported exact derivation). For an orthogonal unitary basis \(\{U_g\}_{g=1}^{d^2}\), \(\operatorname{Tr}(U_g^*U_h)=d\delta_{gh}\), and a full-support random-unitary channel \(\mathcal N_p(X)=\sum_g p_gU_gXU_g^*\), the manuscript solves its Choi objective exactly:
\[
 M(\mathcal N_p)=d^{-4}\sum_g p_g^{-1},\qquad \beta=M^{-1}=\frac{d^4}{\sum_g p_g^{-1}}.
\]
If any probability is zero, the range constraint gives \(M=\infty\) and \(\beta=0\). The algebraic identity for \(M\) is separate from N402; interpreting \(\eta=1-\beta\) as the complete contraction coefficient is conditional on N402.

For a finite projective-Weyl label group \(|G|=d^2\), generator \(L=\sum_{s\in S}\gamma_s(\operatorname{Ad}U_s-\mathrm{id})\), and fixed positive rates whose jumps generate \(G\), let \(\ell(g)\) be directed shortest word length, \(r=\max_g\ell(g)\), and \(c_g=(\ell(g)!)^{-1}\sum_{s_1\cdots s_{\ell(g)}=g}\prod_j\gamma_{s_j}\), with \(c_e=1\). The stated fixed-group asymptotic is
\[
 1-\eta(e^{tL})=\frac{d^4}{\sum_{\ell(g)=r}c_g^{-1}}t^r+O(t^{r+1}).
\]
If the jumps generate a proper subgroup, \(\eta(e^{tL})=1\) at every finite time. For one qubit with \(X,Z\) rates \(a,b>0\), the exact formula is \(1-\eta=(1-e^{-4at})(1-e^{-4bt})\). For \(n\) equal-rate qubits,
\[
\eta_n(t)=1-(1-e^{-4\gamma t})^{2n},\qquad T_n(\epsilon)=-\frac{1}{4\gamma}\log\!\left[1-(1-\epsilon)^{1/(2n)}\right].
\]
The source contrasts this exact transition with the CP-replacer Doeblin baseline; it claims a factor-two difference in the center for this family only. Weighted shortest paths and coefficients can be computed in \(O(|G||S|)\) arithmetic operations by breadth-first search and dynamic programming at fixed group presentation.

Scope: the shortest-path calculation is \(O(|G||S|)\) at fixed group presentation; \(|G|=4^n\) for \(n\) qubits, so this is not a polynomial-in-qubit-count result. The scalar tensor-product formula is exact for the stated family and does not claim a new general quantum mixing theorem.

diagonal restriction manuscript (September 24, 2026) was read. Its
Lemma 3.2 extends to any positive-density exponent r>1: for n weighted
atoms and a legal geometric test capacity, there are at most
`min(n,2+floor((1+1/(r−1))log₂ n))` disjoint coordinate pieces with

```
Σ_j m(u^j)K(u^j)^{r−1}
```

The bound has no dependence on coefficient dynamic range. If weights
are squared complex coefficients and the oscillatory map is linear,
the output norm power is 2r and the resulting grouping loss is
J^{2r−1}; r=3/2 reproduces the source's log² loss. The capacity oracle's
acquisition cost remains separate from the logarithmic piece count.
